blocks.text: Expedia TAAP is Expedia Group’s booking platform for travel advisors: 200,000+ advisors at 38,000+ agencies across 85+ markets, in a business that passed $3 billion in bookings in 2025.
Advisors had powerful booking tools but no way to curate or share what they booked with travelers. I led end-to-end design of a new itinerary builder to close that gap.
In moderated research, every advisor rated the layout clean and professional, and Preview and Share with traveler worked without help. Adoption metrics will follow post-launch.

blocks.text: Advisors could book flights, hotels, and experiences in TAAP, but afterward there was no unified view for the advisor or the traveler. They compiled trip details by hand outside the platform, which added work and made the client experience inconsistent.

blocks.text: I used Figma Make, AI-assisted prototyping, to build a working prototype, so advisors got a realistic experience instead of a click-through. That led to richer qualitative feedback in moderated, 8-task, think-aloud sessions over Zoom with 6 advisors.

groups.heading: What to improve
items: Replace the map with a clickable link
Add more imagery and editable text fields
Pre-populate agency logos, with customization

blocks.text: The findings shaped the final design iterations before handoff. Dev received production-ready UI.

items: Full accessibility annotations
Conditional logic documented
Edge cases covered
Choosing a direction: three concepts in a 2-day sprint, aligned through dot voting and discussion.
Flexibility without clutter: advisors value visual flexibility but also wanted a cleaner layout, so I explored show/hide sections, editable text, and pre-populated logos.
Ideal versus feasible: richer imagery and logo management need a feasibility check with Tech.

blocks.text: The moderated study validated the core interaction model. Adoption metrics will follow post-launch.
